title: §19-003: OS Command Injection & Prototype Pollution Defense
description: Multiple-choice practice questions and deep runtime verification for §19-003 (OS Command Injection & Prototype Pollution Defense).

cards.concept: OS Command Injection & Prototype Pollution Defense: SQL Injection Prevention with Parameterized Queries
cards.question: Why does parameterized query execution prevent SQL injection attacks, whereas string concatenation is vulnerable?

options.text: Parameterized queries encrypt the SQL database file.
The database parses and compiles the SQL query template AST first; parameters are transmitted separately and treated strictly as literal data values, never executable syntax.
Parameterized queries convert user inputs into Base64 strings.
String concatenation only works with integer fields.

cards.explanation: Parameterized queries transmit the query structure and user data separately. The database compiler treats bound parameters purely as literal values, rendering SQL syntax injection impossible.
cards.pitfall: Attempting to sanitize SQL inputs using custom regex replace routines instead of native prepared statements.
cards.citation: OWASP Cheat Sheet Series: SQL Injection Prevention in Node.js

cards.concept: OS Command Injection & Prototype Pollution Defense: NoSQL Operator Injection Defense
cards.question: How can an attacker bypass authentication in a MongoDB/Node.js app using NoSQL injection, and how is it mitigated?

options.text: By sending SQL UNION SELECT statements in headers.
By passing object payloads (e.g. `{ username: 'admin', password: { $gt: '' } }`) in JSON request bodies; mitigate by strictly validating input types (e.g. ensuring password is a string).
By flooding the MongoDB replication log.
By modifying the MongoDB port number.

cards.explanation: If request bodies are passed directly to findOne(), query operators like {$gt: ''} or {$ne: null} evaluate to true. Defend with strict schema validation (Zod, Ajv) verifying string primitives.
cards.pitfall: Using express.json() parser without type verification allows JSON objects where string primitives are expected.
cards.citation: OWASP NoSQL Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet
